title: En face preparation and quantification of aortic surface area covered by atherosclerotic lesions
author: Jan Breslow
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fehtje
materials: Mice are fasted prior to sacrifice.
The mice are weighed prior to euthanasia.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse with isoflurane
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse by administering an overdose of isoflurane; confirm death by the absence of respiration.

steps.title: Open abdomen and collect blood
steps.instruction: Make a midline abdominal incision and add transverse cuts in the abdominal wall to improve perfusate drainage. Collect blood from the abdominal vena cava using a heparinized 1 mL syringe and a 1.5‑inch 22‑gauge needle (needle bent away from the bevel). After collection, push the needle up through the vessel and scrape the intervening section of the vena cava with a scalpel to provide drainage.

substeps.instruction: Midline incision with transverse cuts for drainage
Collect blood with heparinized 1 mL syringe and 1.5‑inch 22‑gauge needle bent away from bevel
Push needle up and scrape vena cava with scalpel

steps.title: Centrifuge blood sample
steps.instruction: Transfer the collected blood into a chilled heparinized tube and centrifuge at 10,000 g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Open thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Open the thoracic cavity by cutting the ribs laterally to the sternum, retract the sternum toward the head, and cut the diaphragm next to the ribs to improve drainage.

steps.title: Perfuse with PBS‑EDTA
steps.instruction: Attach a 22‑gauge needle to a gravity perfusion set, insert it into the left ventricle, and perfuse with PBS containing 0.5 mM EDTA. Continue the flush until perfusate exiting the vena cava is clear of blood.

substeps.instruction: Insert needle into left ventricle
Perfuse PBS + 0.5 mM EDTA until outflow is clear

steps.title: Fix perfusion with PFA‑sucrose‑EDTA
steps.instruction: Switch the perfusion solution to 4 % paraformaldehyde, 7.5 % sucrose, and 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS and perfuse for exactly 15 minutes.

steps.title: Flush PBS‑EDTA to remove fixative
steps.instruction: Briefly flush the animal with PBS/EDTA to remove residual paraformaldehyde from the vessel lumen.

steps.title: Remove organs and weigh tissues
steps.instruction: Remove the ribs, lungs, gastrointestinal and reproductive systems, leaving the heart and kidneys in situ. Weigh the liver and spleen, and save them together with a piece of pancreas in the fixative solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove ribs, lungs, GI and reproductive systems
Weigh liver and spleen
Save liver, spleen, and pancreas piece in fixative

steps.title: Secure mouse on dissection pad
steps.instruction: Tape the mouse to a dissection pad over the front and hind limbs to expose the body cavity.

steps.title: Dissect aorta under microscope
steps.instruction: Under a dissection microscope, dissect the aorta from the heart to 3–5 mm beyond the iliac bifurcation using mini‑Vanna scissors and forceps. Leave all major branching arteries in place except the gastric and hepatic arteries (already severed), and carefully remove all adventitial tissue.

substeps.instruction: Dissect from heart to 3–5 mm past iliac bifurcation
Leave major branches except gastric and hepatic arteries
Remove adventitial tissue

steps.title: Split aorta and isolate segments
steps.instruction: Split the aorta in situ as follows: (a) make a small transverse cut partially through the left iliac artery to insert scissors into the lumen; (b) cut anteriorly to the kidneys, then split the right iliac artery; (c) continue anteriorly, angling at the aortic arch to the inner curve until reaching the heart; (d) remove and weigh the heart; (e) sever the right and common carotid arteries close to the aorta, insert scissors into the right carotid toward the common carotid and make a second cut to lay the arch flat; (f) cut through the carotids and innominate (brachiocephalic) artery until the aorta is split, forming a Y‑shaped arch; (g) sever the renal arteries close to the aorta, remove kidneys from capsules, weigh and save them; (h) sever the iliac arteries 3 mm past the bifurcation and remove the aorta.

substeps.instruction: Transverse cut partially through left iliac artery
Cut anteriorly to kidneys; split right iliac artery
Continue anteriorly, angle at aortic arch to heart
Remove and weigh heart
Sever right and common carotid arteries; second cut to flatten arch
Cut through carotids and innominate artery to split aorta (Y shape)
Sever renal arteries; remove, weigh, and save kidneys
Sever iliac arteries 3 mm past bifurcation; remove aorta

steps.title: Store or pin arteries
steps.instruction: Either store the isolated arteries in PBS at 4 °C (refrigerator) or proceed to pin them for imaging.

steps.title: Pin aorta onto wax pan
steps.instruction: Pin the aortae onto a standard black wax dissection pan using 0.15 mm black anodized pins (Fine Science Tools).

steps.title: Flatten vessels and remove adventitia
steps.instruction: Fill the pan with PBS to prevent dehydration, apply sufficient pins (more in the arch than thoracic/abdominal portions) with slight tension to keep the vessel flat, and remove any remaining adventitia with forceps and scissors.

substeps.instruction: Fill pan with PBS
Pin vessel flat with adequate tension (more pins in arch)
Remove remaining adventitia

steps.title: Stain vessels with Sudan IV
steps.instruction: Stain the vessels: drain PBS, add 70 % ethanol for 5 minutes, drain, add Sudan IV solution for 15 minutes, drain, destain with 80 % ethanol for 3 minutes, drain, rinse under running water, then fill the pan with filtered PBS until the liquid covers the pins completely.

substeps.instruction: Drain PBS, add 70 % ethanol for 5 min
Drain, add Sudan IV for 15 min
Drain, destain with 80 % ethanol for 3 min
Drain, rinse under running water
Fill pan with filtered PBS covering pins

steps.title: Add colored marker bar
steps.instruction: Pin a marker bar containing three 15 mm colored segments next to the vessel to delineate segments; note that arch‑thoracic segments are proximal to the diaphragm (above hepatic artery take‑off) and the abdominal aorta is distal to the diaphragm.

steps.title: Capture images and quantify lesions
steps.instruction: Capture images of the pinned vessels and quantify the area of atherosclerotic lesions using ImagePro software.
